questions.stem:
15. 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
Giraffes may all look identical to us. But none has exactly
the same markings―and certain patterns, especially large,
round patches, can boost their chances of survival before
they turn 4 months old. Biologists can’t decide why giraffes
evolved patches. David Lee at the Nature Institute in South
Carolina and his colleagues examined 258 wild baby Masai
giraffes in Tanzania for clues to the impact of patches on
the animals. They found that calves with fewer, larger spots
had a 17 percent higher chance of survival than those with
more, smaller spots. They also found that those with more
round spots had a 27 percent higher survival rate than those
with elliptical* spots.
* elliptical: 타원형의
choices: the unique ways to raise baby giraffes in Tanzania
different survival rates of baby giraffes by region
the relationship between baby giraffes’ spots and survival rates
scientific methods to conduct research on giraffes’ calves

learning innovation, schools are seeking ways to enhance
school effectiveness.
(A) By assisting teachers to better understand student learning
processes and education policies, schools can improve
teacher effectiveness and address the looming teacher

vital information to teachers in a way that maintains the
teaching quality.
(C) To survive these shortages, schools must put processes in
place before teachers leave and their pedagogical knowledge
leaves with them. Because of the ageing workforce, it is
critical to have effective succession planning in place to
capture this knowledge.

18. 다음 글의 흐름상 어색한 문장은?
Films, like literary works, are powerful instruments of education.
choices:
On a simpler level, English language movies can be used
in classrooms as a vehicle for teaching the English language.

However, the animated film Future Galaxy deals with social
issues from a historical perspective.

But on a higher level,
movies can be used as prisms through which one can learn
how to understand, analyze and “read” complex aspects of the
world humans have constructed and deconstructed in diverse
issues in cultural, social, political, and economic spheres.

Perhaps not most, but many Hollywood movies can be an
insightful source to teach not only American culture, but also
socio-economic-political-historical facets in content-based classes.

questions.stem:
19.
Recently, it has been demonstrated in a series of ingenious
experiments that we even perceive colors through _________
_____________________________________. There are radical
variations in the way languages carve up the spectrum of
visible light; for example, green and blue are distinct colors in
English but are considered shades of the same color in many
languages. And it turns out that the colors that our language
routinely obliges us to treat as distinct can refine our purely
visual sensitivity to certain color differences in reality, so that
our brains are trained to exaggerate the distance between shades
of color if these have different names in our language. As
strange as it may sound, our experience of a Chagall painting
actually depends to some extent on whether our language has
a word for blue.
choices: the reflection of visible light
the comparison of various shades
the lens of our mother tongue
communication among diverse language speakers

Most of us put a lot of stock in what scientists tell us because
we know that scientists reach their conclusions by gathering
and analyzing facts. If someone asked you why you believe
that smoking is bad and jogging is good, or that the earth is
round and the galaxy is flat, you would point to the facts.
You might need to explain that you do not personally know
the facts to which you are pointing, but that you do know
that at some time in the past, a bunch of very earnest people
in white lab coats went out and watched the world, wrote
down what they looked into, analyzed what they wrote down,
and then told the rest of us what to believe. Scientists are
credible because they draw conclusions from _____________,
